title: a re-invoked completion widget reads $compstate[old_list] as `yes` where zsh reads `shown`

spec.completer:
#compdef fzc0000

_sfz_main() {
  _values  '[bracket] in' 'delta[\[bracket\] in say "hi" now]'
}
_sfz_main; _sfz_ret=$?
compadd -U -Q -J _sfzcs -X 'compstate' -- "insert=$compstate[insert]" "list=$compstate[list]" "list_max=$compstate[list_max]" "last_prompt=$compstate[last_prompt]" "to_end=$compstate[to_end]" "old_list=$compstate[old_list]" "exact=$compstate[exact]" "pattern_insert=$compstate[pattern_insert]" "ret=$_sfz_ret"
return $_sfz_ret

observed.notes: Both shells draw the SAME list twice and agree on every other compstate field; the only differing cell is old_list on the SECOND invocation. Doc/Zsh/compwid.yo:320-326 separates the two values: `yes` means a valid old list exists, `shown` means it is also on the screen — and it is on the screen, both shells drew it. The list-choices leg of the `compdef -K` pair is what re-enters completion with a list already displayed. Nothing about this is visible without the compstate probe, which is why the widget axis found it and the screen-diff sweeps did not.

controls.note: same completer, same two presses, through whatever compinit left on TAB: PASSES, so the divergence is the widget, not the completer.
same completer through the BUILTIN list-choices widget: PASSES. The builtin re-invocation sets old_list=shown on both shells.
